answers.answer:
“Usurper victory has two timing windows: at the start of an Exile's turn during Wake, or at the end of round 8 under the endgame priority. From taking Oathkeeper during Act, the normal sequence is next Wake check (not yet Usurper), then flip to Usurper, then win at the following Wake or at the end of round 8 if that arrives first while still Usurper. Losing title prevents this win; retaking resets it to Oathkeeper and restarts the sequence.”
Application: Taking the title during Act does not allow an immediate Usurper win. At the next Wake they are checked before the title flips, then flip to Usurper; their first Wake win check is the following Wake, unless round 8 ends first while they still hold it. If another player takes the title meanwhile, Usurper victory is prevented; retaking starts the sequence over.

“The four Oath names are Supremacy, People, Protection, Devotion.”
“Vision of Conquest matches Oath of Supremacy: rule the most sites. Vision of Rebellion matches Oath of the People: hold People's Favor. Vision of Sanctuary matches Oath of Protection: hold the most relics and banners combined. Vision of Faith matches Oath of Devotion: hold Darkest Secret.”
“Exile must have true Vision revealed and goal completed at Wake, with at least 3 Visions drawn from world deck by all players combined. This is a shared global count, not a requirement for that Exile to draw three personally. Can reveal it earlier but cannot win early. For Conquest/Sanctuary ‘most’ means strictly more than every other player, no ties.”
Application: Those four pairings apply. Every Visionary win also requires the shared world-deck count of at least three and the Exile's revealed Vision and completed goal at Wake. A tie for most does not count.
answers.evidence: Oathkeeper title and four Oaths; Visionary victory

answers.answer:
“Stable regime: at ends of rounds 5, 6 and 7, roll end die only if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper. Ends on respectively 6 / 5–6 / 3–6. Chancellor wins, except a Citizen meeting Successor goal wins alone instead. An Exile Oathkeeper/Usurper prevents the roll.”
Application: Rolls occur only at the ends of rounds 5–7 when an Imperial player (Chancellor or Citizen) is Oathkeeper. The ending results are 6, 5–6, and 3–6 respectively; a winning roll ends the game with the stated Chancellor/Citizen outcome. An Exile Oathkeeper does not permit a roll.

“War exhaustion: round 8 ends automatically. Check in this exact priority:
1. If Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper: Empire wins (Chancellor unless qualified Successor).
2. Otherwise, Exile Usurper wins.
3. Otherwise, qualifying revealed Exile Vision wins. If several qualify, priority Conquest → Rebellion → Sanctuary → Faith.
4. Otherwise Empire wins (Chancellor unless qualified Successor), even if an Exile is only Oathkeeper.
Holding Successor goal never ends game on its own. Resolve it whenever Chancellor would win.”
Application: Apply those tiers in order; a Citizen who qualifies for Successor wins alone instead whenever the tier awards Empire/Chancellor victory. Among simultaneous qualifying Exile Visions, use the stated Vision order.

“Citizen wins only by replacing a Chancellor victory with a Successor win. Use the current Oath to select this separate criterion: Supremacy: Hold more relics and banners combined than the Chancellor and every other Citizen; People: Hold Darkest Secret; Protection: Hold People's Favor; Protection: Hold People's Favor; Devotion: Hold Grand Scepter. A Citizen does not use the Oathkeeper criterion or a Vision goal as their Successor goal. Meeting the Successor criterion alone never ends the game; it matters when the Chancellor would win.”
“Citizens/Chancellor cannot win by true Visions or Usurper.”
Application: The summary supplies Successor goals for Supremacy, People, Protection, and Devotion; its table repeats Protection and has no Sanctuary row, so the Sanctuary goal cannot be answered from this summary. In all cases it says Citizens cannot win through Vision or Usurper and Successor only substitutes for a Chancellor win.
answers.evidence: Citizen succession is a separate test; Visionary victory

answers.answer:
“People's Favor, if held: either put 1 favor from your board on it or return 1 from it to the least-full suit bank (choose among tied banks). Never remove its last favor: at 1, you must add if able; if you have none, nothing happens. If banner is already Mob-side, repeat this choice once. Afterwards, if it has 6+ favor, flip to Mob. A banner becoming Mob at this last step does not retroactively repeat the payment that Wake.”
Application: Resolve once if held, and a second time only if already Mob at Wake start. Do not remove the last favor; add if possible or do nothing if unable. Check the 6+ threshold after the choice(s), so flipping at the end does not create a second payment that Wake.

“Rest: mandatory order
1. Return favor on denizens/edifices to suit-matching banks.
2. Return secrets on denizens/edifices/relics to your board. Flip facedown secrets on your board faceup.
3. Exile/Chancellor refresh Supply to the space showing their warbands remaining in personal bank. For Chancellor: 18+ gives 6 Supply, 11–17 gives 5, 4–10 gives 4, 0–3 gives 3. For Exile: 9+ gives 6, 4–8 gives 5, 0–3 gives 4. Citizen refreshes to the exact Chancellor marker space, including leftmost, not by counting purple warbands.
4. Save remaining unspent Supply: move marker one extra space left per unspent Supply, capped at leftmost (7 Supply).
5. Optional Rest powers, each once in chosen order.”
Application: Follow those five steps in order. A Citizen copies the Chancellor's exact Supply marker location. Saving unspent Supply is the extra leftward movement after refresh, one space for every remaining Supply, up to the leftmost cap; Rest powers follow and are optional.

“Choose either world deck or your pawn's region discard pile, never both. Discard-pile Search costs 2. World-deck Search costs 2 at zero Visions drawn, 3 at 1–2, and 4 at 3–5; Darkest Secret replaces the world-deck cost with 2. Other applicable modifiers still apply.
Draw 3 cards, taking fewer only if the source runs out, a world-deck Vision stops you, or a modifier reduces the draw. You cannot voluntarily stop early. From world deck, draw one at a time, with no required public showing of drawn card fronts. If a Vision is drawn, announce that a Vision was drawn (not necessarily which Vision), stop immediately and increase Visions Drawn by 1. Drawing Visions from a discard does not stop drawing or advance the track. If source empties, draw only what remains; no reshuffle is implied.”
Application: Choose only one source. The quoted costs vary by source and Visions Drawn, with Darkest Secret substitution and other modifiers still applying. A Vision from world deck is announced, ends the draw immediately, and advances the track; a discard-pile Vision does neither, so Search continues toward three cards unless source/reduction ends it.

“Facedown atop next region's pile: Cradle → Provinces → Hinterland → Cradle, ordering multiple discards as you choose. For cards in hand/advisers, discard based on your pawn’s region: pawn in Cradle means Provinces pile; pawn in Provinces means Hinterland pile; pawn in Hinterland means Cradle pile. Never use the same-region pile. When discarding a card at a site in another region, apply that cycle to the card’s region instead of your pawn’s. Favor on discarded cards immediately returns to matching bank; their secrets go to acting player's board facedown.”
Application: Ordinary hand/adviser discards use the next-region cycle keyed to your pawn's region. A card discarded from a remote site instead uses that card site's region to pick the next pile. Its favor immediately returns to its matching bank and secrets go facedown on the acting player's board.

“Adviser: play faceup or facedown. Up to 3 total, including facedown; before exceeding limit discard an adviser, subject to locked cards. If the incoming card changes the adviser limit, check against the new limit before playing it; use the lowest of multiple limits. Later options: as a minor action you may play a facedown adviser faceup to a legal destination or discard that facedown adviser; you cannot discard a faceup adviser at will. Faceup advisers can be discarded only when another rule permits or requires it. Facedown cards have no suit, restriction banner or power; any card, including site-only cards and Visions, can be held facedown.”
“True Vision: Exile only, faceup in Revealed Vision slot, replacing and discarding old revealed Vision. Not an adviser.”
Application: Facedown advisers count toward the limit but have no active suit/restriction/power; later, a minor action may legally play one faceup or discard it. Faceup advisers are not freely discardable. An Exile playing a true Vision faceup puts it in the separate Vision slot and discards the previously revealed Vision.
answers.evidence: Search options: Adviser and True Vision

answers.answer:
“Muster — 1 Supply. Place 1 favor on an empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn's site (no favor or secrets already). Gain 2 warbands from personal bank onto board; Citizens gain purple. Relics/ruins are ineligible. Rule is not required, and ruling a remote site does not allow remote Muster.”
“Trade — 1 Supply. Choose an empty denizen/intact edifice at your pawn's site; no relics/ruins. Choose:
- Put 1 secret on card: gain 1 favor plus 1 per matching faceup adviser, from that card's suit bank.
- Put 2 favor on card: gain 1 shared-bank secret per matching faceup adviser. With no matching advisers gain zero secrets.
Facedown advisers never match. Finite source exhaustion gives only available favor/warbands; secrets are unlimited. Costs remain payable even if a gain is reduced to zero.”
Application: Both actions cost 1 Supply and require an eligible empty denizen/intact edifice at your pawn's site. Muster pays 1 favor and gains two personal-bank warbands onto board (purple for Citizen). Trade's secret payment yields card-suit-bank favor starting at 1 plus matching faceup adviser count; its 2-favor payment yields one shared-bank secret per matching faceup adviser. With no match, the latter yields zero secrets but the cost remains.

“Recover — 1 Supply plus target cost. Recover 1 facedown relic at your site or either banner from anywhere, including yourself or shared bank. Relics held by players or in Reliquary cannot be recovered. Pay relic's site cost (3 favor to indicated bank, burn 2 favor, burn 1 secret or burn 2 secrets), then hold it faceup in personal bank.”
“People's Favor: pay any amount of favor strictly greater than its current favor. Put paid favor on banner; distribute old favor singly to suit banks, starting at any chosen bank, then moving away from the world deck through successive banks and wrapping as needed (the printed bank order). Do not return the old favor to the previous holder. Flip it to normal side if Mob. No seizure penalty when recovering.”
“Darkest Secret: pay any amount of secrets strictly greater than current secrets. Put paid secrets on it; new holder takes 1 old secret, previous holder takes rest. Recovering from self returns all old secrets to yourself; from shared bank, remainder stays in bank.”
Application: Pay 1 Supply plus the relic's printed site cost for a facedown relic at your site; held/Reliquary relics are ineligible. A banner may be recovered from anywhere by strictly outbidding its current resource count. People's Favor's old resources are distributed to suit banks per the order described, without seizure penalty; Darkest Secret distributes one old secret to the new holder and the rest to previous holder, with self/shared-bank exceptions quoted above.

“To recover from another player, there must be at least one suited card at their pawn’s site whose suit matches none of their faceup advisers. One mismatching card is enough even if every other site card matches; the condition is not that all site cards must be unmatched. Empty sites and ruin-only sites protect it. Ruins and facedown advisers have no suit. If holder has no faceup advisers but a suited site card exists, it is recoverable; the printed Law's contrary parenthetical is erroneous. Recovering from self or shared bank ignores this protection.”
Application: It is recoverable from another player when at least one suited card at their pawn's site is unmatched by all their faceup advisers. With no faceup advisers, a suited site card meets the test. No suited card means protected: this includes no cards and a ruin-only site.
answers.evidence: Darkest Secret protection, corrected by official errata

answers.answer:
“Choose defender: any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there. If no player rules your site, you may choose bandits.”
“Declare targets, form pools: at least one target must be at your pawn's site; if defender rules that site you must target it. May target any of defender's sites anywhere on map (1 defense die each). If defender's pawn is at your site, may also target any of their relics (printed defense dice), banners (dice equal resources on banner), or pawn-and-favor together (2 dice). A co-located defender's relic target satisfies the local-target requirement.”
Application: Select an eligible other player, or bandits only if no player rules your site. At least one target must be local, with the additional mandatory local-site target if defender rules your site. You may add any defender site anywhere. If the defender's pawn is at your site, their relic, banner, or pawn-and-favor may be targeted; a relic there itself satisfies the local requirement.

“Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in attacking force. Apply relevant modifiers and mandatory title defense bonus: Oathkeeper +1 defense die, Usurper +2.”
“Roll defense: shields rolled, doubled for each double-symbol (multipliers stack ×2, ×4, ×8...), plus all defending warbands at targeted sites, plus defender's board force if their pawn is at attacker site or any targeted site. Doubles multiply shields only, not warbands. Bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site.”
“Roll attack: each skull immediately kills 1 own force warband. Count full swords; each pair of hollow swords adds 1, leftover single adds zero. May sacrifice own surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice exactly enough to win, never excess. Attacker wins only if attack strictly exceeds defense; tie or lower means defender wins.”
Application: Attack dice cannot exceed attacking-force warbands; compute defense from rolled shields after doubling plus eligible defending warbands and applicable board force, with bandit site addition. Resolve skull casualties immediately, score full swords plus one per pair of hollow swords, and any sacrifice must be precisely the amount needed to make attack exceed defense. A tie is a defender win.

“Resolve defeat before taking targets: on attacker victory, the defender first kills half of the warbands in its defending force, rounded down, returning the rest to board. On defender victory, the attacker kills half its remaining attacking force, rounded down, leaving the survivors on its board; bandits cannot be killed and go into hiding. Resolve defeated battle-plan effects.”
“If attacker won: may place any number, including zero, of surviving force warbands on any targeted sites. Zero leaves site to bandits unless another power applies. Take all targeted relics/banners. For a seized banner (taken any way except Recover), burn 2 of its resources to minimum 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn-and-favor targeted, may force defender to travel to a legal chosen site for no Supply, and independently may burn half their board favor, rounded down. Respect site travel restrictions. Shrouded Wood overrides the attacker’s destination choice if its enemy ruler chooses where the pawn must go.”
“Finish battle-plan effects for either winner: defeated effects occur immediately after defeat casualties (step 6). If attacker won, resolve targets (step 7), then attacker’s victorious effects.”
Application: Following attacker victory, first inflict defender force casualties and defeated-plan effects; next resolve attacker targets. The attacker can place zero surviving warbands (leaving sites to bandits absent another power), takes all targeted relics and banners, and seized banners incur the two-resource burn-to-minimum-one penalty and People's Favor flips Mob. Targeting pawn-and-favor separately permits banishment to a legal site at no Supply and burning half board favor rounded down; obey travel restrictions, including Shrouded Wood's destination override. Then resolve victorious attacker plans and end-discard plans as specified in the Campaign procedure.

“A Citizen attacking Chancellor/another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign. If Chancellor attacks Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for it.”
“When an Imperial player defends, Chancellor automatically joins as Ally. Other non-attacking Citizens may join with defender's permission if their pawn is at attacker site or any targeted site.”
“Share powers as one defending side: their ‘you,’ ‘your enemy,’ and ‘defender’ mean the whole side, while ‘your site’/‘your board’ still mean each user’s own location/board. This shares the Oathkeeper defense bonus even outside Supremacy. Allied board warbands add defense only if pawn at attacker site or targeted site.”
“Defender/Allies may use plans at Imperial sites and their own advisers, not other players' advisers. Each shared battle plan may be used once total per Campaign by one user, who pays its cost.”
“An intra-Empire Campaign does not make all Citizens non-Imperial; only the specified attacker/defender loses that status temporarily.”
Application: Imperial defense adds Chancellor automatically and may add eligible Citizens with defender permission, with side-wide powers and defense contributions under the stated location conditions. The one shared plan can be used only once total, paid by its user. A Citizen attacking an Imperial opponent, or a Citizen attacked by Chancellor, is non-Imperial only for that Campaign; this does not strip all Citizens of status in an intra-Empire conflict.
answers.evidence: Imperial defense; Campaign steps 1 and Imperial defense

answers.answer:
“Move pawn to any different site, not necessarily an adjacent slot; site garrisons stay put. Board warbands travel with your pawn in the sense that they stay on your board.”
“Travel [base costs]: Cradle to Cradle 1, Provinces 2, Hinterland 4; Provinces to Cradle 2, Provinces 2, Hinterland 2; Hinterland to Cradle 4, Provinces 2, Hinterland 3.”
“Reveal facedown destination; put printed favor/secrets there from shared bank and printed number of relics beside it facedown from relic deck. Travel cost order: fixed-number cost first, then other increases/decreases. Free Travel is the final override: any applicable power saying ‘spend no Supply’ makes Supply payment zero even if another power increases it. This general rule applies to all Travel, including banishment, not only named site examples. Site entry restrictions still apply unless ignored by name/power.”
Application: Pay the region-pair base cost shown above before applying increases/decreases; any applicable spend-no-Supply power then sets payment to zero. Reveal and stock a facedown destination as quoted. These cost rules also apply to banishment; entry restrictions remain unless expressly ignored.

“The Grand Scepter cannot make an offer on the turn its current holder took it. In later turns it may offer any Exile, including itself. Must promise exactly one Reliquary relic; may additionally negotiate a binding exchange of favor, secrets, banners and non-Reliquary relics. May let recipient peek at Reliquary relics. Other binding-deal powers cannot trade Reliquary relics.”
“Acceptance: flip to Citizen; replace all own warbands on board/map with purple. If insufficient purple, new Citizen chooses which to remove and which to replace. Discard revealed Vision, flip own Usurper title to Oathkeeper, end Act if own turn, and refresh to full leftmost Supply. Exchange promised pieces; Chancellor gains the newly uncovered mandatory Reliquary modifier.”
Application: Only the Scepter holder can offer during play, and not on the turn they acquired it. An offer can go to any Exile including the holder, and must promise exactly one Reliquary relic; other exchanges of favor, secrets, banners, and non-Reliquary relics may also be negotiated as binding terms. Acceptance performs the listed status and piece conversions, exchanges promised pieces, and ends the new Citizen's Act if acceptance occurs on their own turn.
answers.evidence: Citizenship and exile during play: Offer; Acceptance

answers.answer:
“Vow an Oath: won by Vision alone → next Oath matches that Vision. Any other way or multiple victory methods → choose any Oath except current one. Save goal in World Box.”
“Free Chronicle Citizenship (ignore normal offers): no Reliquary relic, resource payment or Scepter permission is required. If winner Exile, flip all Citizen boards, including boxed, to Exile, then may offer Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped. Each accepting Exile must do both: flip their board to Citizen and replace every garrison at each site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband at that site, regardless of the old garrison size. Winner cannot offer themself Chronicle Citizenship.”
“Rebuild world deck: shuffle all denizens remaining in play (not those retained at sites/Archive/Dispossessed). Top stack 10 denizens + 2 random Visions = 12; middle 15 denizens + remaining 3 Visions = 18; remaining denizens bottom. Save in Archive World Deck section. Chronicle aid's printed ‘12 denizens + 2’ is incorrect; do not make a 14-card top stack.”
Application: Set the next Oath from the victory method rule; Chronicle Citizenship follows the special free turnover and acceptance requirements. Rebuild the deck in the specified stacks. The top stack has 10 denizens plus 2 Visions, twelve total; the summary explicitly identifies “12 denizens + 2” on the aid as erroneous.
